clusters.rule: User-facing text in strings.json must follow Home Assistant string style: sentence case with only the brand or product name capitalised and spelled the same way as the neighbouring entries, `for example` spelled out instead of e.g., no slash-joined noun pairs, and literal example values wrapped in backticks rather than quotes.
clusters.trigger: An added or changed strings.json value uses title case or capitalises a common noun mid-sentence while neighbouring entries are sentence case, spells the brand differently from existing entries in the same file, contains a slash-joined noun pair or e.g., or quotes an example value.
clusters.rationale: Every integration's strings feed the same UI and the same translation pipeline, so reviewers hold new entries to the style the surrounding entries already use rather than letting each integration drift.

clusters.rule: Entity names must come from strings.json: give every new entity an _attr_translation_key (or a description translation_key) with a matching entry under `entity`, and do not also set a literal name on that description.
clusters.trigger: A new entity or EntityDescription sets _attr_device_class or a literal name with no translation_key, declares both translation_key= and name=, or a snapshot shows original_name/object_id_base as None with an entity_id equal to the bare device or container slug.
clusters.rationale: A name written in code cannot be translated and collapses the entity_id onto the device name; reviewers expect the translation key to be the single source of the displayed name.

clusters.rule: strings.json and the code must correspond in both directions and in the same PR: every translation key, error key, entity name, enum state and options value the code can reference must have an entry, and no entry may be added that nothing references or removed while code still uses it.
clusters.trigger: A diff adds exception, error or entity translation keys that no code references, adds a raise path nothing can reach, adds new device-class/enum state constants or options values without the corresponding strings.json keys, or deletes a `name` under a key that code still sets as translation_key.
clusters.rationale: The frontend falls back to the raw key when an entry is missing, and a stale entry hides which messages are actually reachable, so reviewers check both directions on every strings.json change.

clusters.rule: An exception translation key must be written for the specific failure that raises it: do not reuse one key across unrelated exception types or borrow a service/action key for the coordinator update path - split or broaden the key instead, and pass the underlying error text as its placeholder rather than a hardcoded generic string.
clusters.trigger: A raise site uses a translation_key whose strings.json message names a different or narrower failure than the exception being raised - one key reused for several exception classes, or _async_update_data raising UpdateFailed with a service error key and a literal placeholder.
clusters.rationale: The translated message is the only thing the user sees, so a borrowed key tells them the wrong thing about what failed.

clusters.rule: Missing or None device data must be handled explicitly and surface as unknown: guard coordinator.data, list indexing and device lookups before dereferencing them, and return None rather than crashing, raising UpdateFailed, or collapsing the absent value into the false/off branch.
clusters.trigger: A native_value/is_on/available property or an EntityDescription value_fn dereferences self.coordinator.data, indexes a library result or looks a device up by id with no None or membership guard; or a state expression such as `result.get(key) == "0"`, `bool(data.get(key, False))` or `"a" if flag else "b"` turns a possible None into a boolean.
clusters.rationale: Devices drop fields and go offline; reviewers want the entity to report unknown so users can see the data is missing, rather than a traceback in the log or a confidently wrong `off`.

clusters.rule: Anything derived from device or coordinator data must be recomputed on every update path rather than frozen at construction: populate attributes and capability mappings from one shared method called from both __init__ and the update callback, assign on all sibling branches of a conditional, and clear a cached value when the new payload no longer contains it, before writing state.
clusters.trigger: An entity __init__ assigns a subset of the _attr_* values its update callback assigns or caches a dict built from device status/capabilities; a state-derivation method sets an attribute in one branch and leaves it untouched in the elif/else; or an update callback calls async_write_ha_state on an early-return branch without resetting the value or availability.
clusters.rationale: A value computed once in __init__ or on only one branch goes stale the moment the device changes, and users see an attribute that never updates.

clusters.rule: Compose _attr_unique_id and DeviceInfo identifiers from every identifier that can vary - the parent node, hub or device id alongside the config entry id and the description key, plus a per-entity suffix - whenever the resource or entity is only unique inside its parent.
clusters.trigger: A unique_id or identifiers f-string is built from only the config entry id/unique id plus a description key or resource name for a resource enumerated per device, node or hub; or a comprehension creates several entities of the same class from one device object with the unique_id derived only from the device id.
clusters.rationale: Registry collisions silently drop entities, so reviewers check that every component of the identity that can repeat ends up in the id.

clusters.rule: Key long-lived caches and lookup dictionaries by a stable identifier such as the unique_id, never by a value that changes at runtime such as the entity's display name or its entity_id.
clusters.trigger: A module-level or hass.data dict is keyed by a human-readable name variable, or indexed by entity.entity_id in async_added_to_hass and deleted by entity.entity_id in async_will_remove_from_hass.
clusters.rationale: Users rename entities and devices, and a cache keyed on the display name or entity_id silently leaks entries and stops matching after the first rename.

clusters.rule: Sensor entity descriptions must set suggested_display_precision explicitly, alongside the native and suggested units, instead of relying on the device-class default.
clusters.trigger: A SensorEntityDescription declares device_class/state_class and a native unit for a numeric value but omits suggested_display_precision.
clusters.rationale: The device-class default rarely matches the precision the device actually reports, and the registry options it produces are what the entity snapshots pin.

clusters.rule: Declare entity attributes through the _attr_* attributes or an EntityDescription only: not as a @property returning a constant, not as a bare un-prefixed class attribute, and never duplicated into a legacy private attribute alongside its _attr_ counterpart.
clusters.trigger: An entity class body contains `translation_key = ...` without the _attr_ prefix and outside an EntityDescription, defines a supported_features property returning a constant flag combination, or assigns both self._attr_name and self._name to the same value.
clusters.rationale: The _attr_ family is the mechanism the base Entity actually reads; anything else either has no effect at all or duplicates state that then drifts apart.

clusters.rule: async_turn_on must never leave the device off: a zero percentage or brightness must be clamped to the minimum running value or treated as if it had not been supplied so the default applies, rather than mapped onto the device's off state.
clusters.trigger: async_turn_on branches on `percentage is not None` and forwards 0 to a setter that maps it to an OFF mode, or converts ATTR_BRIGHTNESS with a truthiness guard such as `if brightness:` so a 0 reaches the device.
clusters.rationale: A turn_on that switches the device off contradicts the platform contract and leaves the entity state and the device disagreeing.

clusters.rule: Encode device values through the semantics the pinned library declares - its enum members and its documented units - never through magic integers, divisors or thresholds written into integration code.
clusters.trigger: An entity description literal contains a state or value mapping keyed by bare integers instead of library enum members, or integration code divides, scales or range-checks a raw library value against a literal before assigning it.
clusters.rationale: The library owns the device protocol; a constant copied into the integration goes silently wrong when the library changes it, and a reviewer cannot tell whether it was ever right.

clusters.rule: Do not feature-detect on the integration's own pinned library with hasattr/getattr/callable: the manifest pins the version, so call the API directly and unconditionally - including registering update listeners in async_added_to_hass through async_on_remove.
clusters.trigger: A setup or platform filter such as `if callable(getattr(node, "method", None))` applied to objects from the requirement package, or an async_added_to_hass that wraps add_update_listener or a similar subscription in `if hasattr(...)` while sibling platforms register it unconditionally.
clusters.rationale: A pinned requirement means the attribute is either present or the pin is wrong; the guard only hides a typing or version mistake, and here it silently skips the subscription so the entity never updates.

clusters.rule: Handle each failure class on its own branch: only an authentication failure (401) may start a reauth flow, and it must raise its own message saying reauthentication is required; an authorization failure (403) must raise ConfigEntryError because new credentials cannot fix it; and connection, timeout and server-side failures must be reported the way the sibling setup path reports them.
clusters.trigger: An except clause groups an authentication error together with connection/transport errors into one HomeAssistantError, or a config-flow/coordinator branch converts a broad API exception or any 4xx into a specific abort/error key or calls async_start_reauth without inspecting the status code.
clusters.rationale: Reauth prompts the user for credentials, so pointing it at a network outage or a permissions problem sends them down a path that cannot possibly succeed.

clusters.rule: A domain's triggers.yaml, conditions.yaml and services.yaml must describe the full surface the implementation accepts - every field the schema takes, including the common `for` duration, and every domain the feature applies to, including the matching input_* helper domains - and a refactor may add entries but must never drop or rename existing ones.
clusters.trigger: A triggers.yaml / conditions.yaml / services.yaml diff removes or omits a field the schema still supports, or a target entity selector names a single domain where the corresponding helper domain (input_select, input_boolean, input_number, ...) also implements the behaviour.
clusters.rationale: These YAML descriptors are the only thing the UI editor sees, so anything missing from them is unreachable for users even though the code supports it.

clusters.rule: Normalize a device- or payload-supplied unit before it reaches the entity: map it onto Home Assistant's canonical units for the entity's device_class, fall back to the entity description's default when it is unrecognized, and turn an empty string into None rather than passing it through.
clusters.trigger: A payload, MQTT property or discovery value is assigned directly to self._attr_native_unit_of_measurement or an entity description unit without mapping it through the canonical unit constants, including a `"unit": ""` value carried from a fixture or datapoint.
clusters.rationale: An unrecognized or empty unit breaks unit conversion and long-term statistics, and surfaces to users as an entity with an empty unit_of_measurement.

clusters.rule: Resolve the config entry a service call targets with homeassistant.helpers.service.async_get_config_entry rather than hand-rolled lookups, so a missing, wrong-domain or unloaded entry raises ServiceValidationError instead of a generic or unhandled error.
clusters.trigger: An integration service handler defines its own _async_get_config_entry-style function over hass.config_entries, or resolves an entry and then raises HomeAssistantError, asserts, or proceeds without a ServiceValidationError path when it is missing or not loaded.
clusters.rationale: The core helper already produces the translated ServiceValidationError users expect for this case, and every integration re-implementing it produces a different message for the same situation.

clusters.rule: A new entity platform module, or a new entity description added to an existing descriptions tuple, must come with tests whose fixture data actually creates the entity and exercises each value its mapping declares, plus regenerated and committed snapshot files; any hard-coded expected-entity list must follow the order the descriptions are iterated during setup.
clusters.trigger: A diff adds homeassistant/components/<domain>/<platform>.py or appends an EntityDescription (including a state_mapping/options dict) without a matching added or extended tests/components/<domain>/test_<platform>.py, updated fixtures, or regenerated snapshot.
clusters.rationale: An untested description is indistinguishable from a typo, and the snapshot is what proves the entity, its unit and its state actually materialise for the fixture device.

clusters.rule: Commit only .ambr snapshots produced by running pytest --snapshot-update against the current code: never hand-write, hand-append or hand-edit snapshot blocks or their parametrization ids, and regenerate rather than leaving stale duplicate entries for one unique_id.
clusters.trigger: A diff to tests/components/*/snapshots/*.ambr deviates from generator output - a manually written EntityRegistryEntrySnapshot block, a duplicated `# ---` divider, a bracketed id that does not match the parametrize source values, or two entries sharing a unique_id under different entity_ids.
clusters.rationale: A hand-edited snapshot asserts what the author believed rather than what the code produces, which is the one thing the snapshot exists to catch.

clusters.rule: A value that already has a name must be imported, not restated: use the integration's and core's own constants and helpers (DOMAIN, CONF_*, STATE_*, identifier helpers) wherever a literal would otherwise be written, in tests as well as in code, and define a value used by more than one module once - in the integration's const.py for code, in the shared test module for tests.
clusters.trigger: A raw literal such as the domain name, `unavailable`, or a config/option key appears in a module, test or conftest where the integration or homeassistant.const already defines a constant; an identifier is recomputed inline where the integration has a helper; or a constant, command map or tuning literal (delay, timeout, threshold, TEST_*) is added to a second module while the same value is already named elsewhere in that integration.
clusters.rationale: Duplicated literals drift apart silently, so reviewers ask for a single definition that a rename or a retune cannot leave half the code and tests behind on.

clusters.rule: Migration tests must start from a realistic pre-migration state and cover every variant the migration can encounter: seed the entity registry with the entities an existing install would already have and assert they are re-associated with the new device or subentry, and exercise each stored value shape and each unique_id format the integration has produced, without one format's pattern matching another's ids.
clusters.trigger: A diff modifies async_migrate_entry, an import step, or normalization of stored config entry data while its tests add no case for the newly handled input variants, derive old-format unique_ids by string slicing or suffix matching, skip entries where a component such as the channel is None, or assert only that subentries and devices were created without registering the old entities beforehand.
clusters.rationale: A migration runs once per install and cannot be re-run, so an untested variant leaves those users with orphaned entities and no way back.

clusters.rule: When code newly depends on optional or loosely typed payload fields, add a test with a reduced payload - fields omitted, null, or carrying an unexpected value - asserting that setup does not raise, that only the always-available entities are created, that the value helpers return None instead of raising, and that absent data reads as unknown rather than as false or zero.
clusters.trigger: A platform's async_setup_entry gains `if <key> in data` guards around entity creation, new value_fn helpers introduce `return None` paths, a property returns bool | None, or payload data is fed into a SensorDeviceClass/SensorStateClass lookup, while the fixtures contain only fully populated, well-formed payloads.
clusters.rationale: Real devices omit fields and firmware versions differ; the fully populated fixture is the case that already works, so the degraded payload is the one worth a test.

clusters.rule: A branch the diff adds must be tested in every outcome it can take, not only the one that motivated the change: the rejection as well as the acceptance, the success path as well as the failure path, the suppressed case as well as the reported one, and each distinct error or translation variant the new code can produce.
clusters.trigger: A diff adds a conditional - an auth guard such as @require_admin on a view, a legacy vs non-legacy platform-loading branch, a device-quirk `available` override, a config-flow fallback path, a new hassfest validation, a caller-is-a-built-in-integration check, or a repair issue that selects among translation keys - while the accompanying tests exercise only one side of it.
clusters.rationale: The untested side is exactly the behaviour the change introduces, so reviewers here treat a half-covered branch as an untested change.

clusters.rule: When shared code gains a branch, add coverage for every consumer of it, not only the one the change was written for - each flow that calls a shared config-flow helper including reauth, and each subclass of a modified trigger or helper base class, including subclasses whose semantics the change would alter.
clusters.trigger: A diff adds a fallback or conditional inside validate_input() or another helper shared by the user/discovery/reauth steps, or changes an EntityTriggerBase-style base class, while the test diff touches only one calling flow or only one subclass implementation.
clusters.rationale: Shared helpers are shared precisely because several callers depend on them, and the caller nobody tested is the one that breaks.

clusters.rule: A parametrized test must span the whole input space the implementation accepts, including its edge and negative values: every supported entity domain plus an unsupported one proving it does not match, and the combined-flags and zero/empty value alongside the individual enum members.
clusters.trigger: A new or edited parametrization lists only individual enum members where the code interprets bitwise capability flags, or only one supported domain (e.g. only `person`) for a trigger or condition that also handles others, with no unsupported-entity or empty-value case.
clusters.rationale: Interpretation bugs live in the combined and empty cases, and a matcher with no negative case cannot show that it stops matching everything else.

clusters.rule: Every fixture, fixture file, module-level TEST_* constant, test-signature parameter and parametrization added must be consumed by a test in the same PR, or removed - including a parametrize over a fixture name that the test signature does not take.
clusters.trigger: A diff adds a conftest fixture, a file under tests/components/*/fixtures/, a helper such as init_*_integration, or a test-signature parameter that no test in the diff references; leaves one behind after the test that used it changed; or applies @pytest.mark.parametrize over a fixture name to a test whose signature omits that name.
clusters.rationale: Scaffolding nothing reads is dead weight the next contributor has to reason about, and a parametrization the signature ignores runs the same test twice while looking like coverage.

clusters.rule: A test's name and docstring must describe exactly the platform, service, failure and outcome its body actually exercises: patch the dependency so the named path really happens - a failing side_effect for a failure test rather than a benign empty result - and when a copied or parametrized test disagrees with its body, fix whichever of the two is wrong before merge.
clusters.trigger: A module or test docstring names a different platform, service or exception than the file/body asserts, including a docstring copied from a neighbouring test or one describing only a subset of the parametrize list; or a test named for a startup/discovery failure patches the helper to return an empty result and asserts a generic abort reason.
clusters.rationale: Reviewers read the name and docstring to know what is covered, so a test whose body does something else leaves the named path uncovered and nobody notices.

clusters.rule: A test double must match the real callable it replaces: patch coroutine functions with new_callable=AsyncMock and synchronous ones with MagicMock, never spec a whole library object as AsyncMock when it also exposes synchronous listener or registration methods, and give replacement functions *args and **kwargs so they accept the arguments the integration passes.
clusters.trigger: patch("<library>.<Class>.<async_method>", return_value=...) without new_callable=AsyncMock; a patch, AsyncMock(spec=...) or fixture annotation whose sync-vs-async kind does not match the awaited-ness of the target in the integration code; or a zero-argument stub substituted for a library method the integration calls with arguments.
clusters.rationale: A mismatched double either hands back a non-awaitable MagicMock or throws on the real call signature, so the test passes or fails for a reason unrelated to the code under test.

clusters.rule: Drive and inspect an integration through its public test helpers and registries - inject_bluetooth_service_info, the entity registry - never through private coordinator callbacks or internal hass.data structures.
clusters.trigger: A test calls coordinator._async_handle_bluetooth_event(...) or another underscore-prefixed coordinator callback to simulate an advertisement, or does hass.data["entity_components"]["<platform>"].get_entity(entity_id) to inspect an entity object.
clusters.rationale: Tests written against internals pin implementation details instead of behaviour, and break on every refactor the public surface would have survived.

clusters.rule: Advance coordinator intervals with the freezer - freezer.tick(...) followed by async_fire_time_changed(hass) - rather than a separately computed dt_util.utcnow() + timedelta timestamp, and never one captured before the config entries were set up.
clusters.trigger: async_fire_time_changed(hass, dt_util.utcnow() + timedelta(...)) in a test that also uses the freezer fixture, or a `now` assigned before async_setup_component / hass.config_entries.async_setup and then used as the base for the fired time.
clusters.rationale: A timestamp taken before setup can land before the timer the entity scheduled, so the refresh never fires and the test asserts on stale state or passes for the wrong reason.

clusters.rule: Tooling that generates a pull request body must read the checked-in .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md and keep its instructional HTML comments and mandated section text, instead of embedding its own copy of the template.
clusters.trigger: Agent instructions, scripts or docs that produce a PR body contain a hardcoded copy of the template, or instruct that all HTML comments be stripped from it.
clusters.rationale: The template is the single source of truth and changes over time; a duplicated copy silently drifts, and the comments carry the instructions contributors are supposed to follow.

clusters.rule: Keep types-* stub packages out of automated dependency bumps; a stub pin must be changed only together with the upstream runtime dependency whose version it types.
clusters.trigger: A renovate/dependabot config adds or removes a types-* entry from the ignore list, or a types-* pin is bumped with no matching bump of its upstream package.
clusters.rationale: A stub package that runs ahead of the library it types describes an API the pinned runtime does not have, so mypy validates against the wrong surface.

clusters.rule: Guard CI jobs and steps that consume repository secrets with an `if:` condition so they are skipped rather than failed when the secret is unavailable, notably on pull_request runs from forks.
clusters.trigger: A workflow job or step references secrets.* (or runs a validate_*_secret script) with no condition on the secret being present or on the event not being a fork pull request.
clusters.rationale: Fork PRs never receive secrets, so an unguarded job turns every external contribution red for a reason the contributor cannot fix.

clusters.rule: Write all comments, docstrings and identifiers in English; non-English text must be translated before merge.
clusters.trigger: An added line under homeassistant/components/ contains a comment or docstring with non-English text, for example CJK characters.
clusters.rationale: The codebase is maintained by an international community, and only user-facing strings go through the translation system - source text has to be readable by every reviewer.

clusters.rule: Every status in quality_scale.yaml must match what the integration actually implements: never mark a rule `done` without the code that satisfies it, never leave `todo` on a rule that is already implemented, and mark rules the integration structurally cannot satisfy as `exempt` with a comment whose justification agrees with manifest.json.
clusters.trigger: A quality_scale.yaml diff sets or keeps a status that the integration's source contradicts - `done` with no implementation, `todo` alongside the implementation, or an `exempt` comment (e.g. about not polling) that conflicts with the manifest iot_class.
clusters.rationale: The quality scale is the promise the integration makes to users and to the reviewer checklist; a status that does not describe the code makes the whole scale untrustworthy.

clusters.rule: Normalize every MAC or Bluetooth address with homeassistant.helpers.device_registry.format_mac before using it as a config entry unique id, a device identifier, or a device registry connection; never hand-roll upper/lowercasing or colon insertion.
clusters.trigger: A MAC or Bluetooth address is built with .upper()/.lower(), slicing or ':'.join(...) and passed to async_set_unique_id, device identifiers, or a CONNECTION_NETWORK_MAC / CONNECTION_BLUETOOTH connections set.
clusters.rationale: Different discovery sources deliver the same address in different casing and separators; only the shared helper produces the canonical form, so hand-rolled formatting creates duplicate devices and broken unique-id matching.

clusters.rule: A service handler may only index call.data with keys declared in the voluptuous schema registered for that specific service; read optional or per-service fields with call.data.get() and handle the missing case.
clusters.trigger: A shared service handler branches on an attribute constant and reads call.data[ATTR_X] where ATTR_X is not part of the schema of the service being executed.
clusters.rationale: Only the registered schema guarantees a key is present; indexing a key another service declares raises KeyError on a perfectly valid call.

clusters.rule: Create entities only for the capabilities and datapoints the specific device instance actually reports, and gate each conditional entity on the very flag or data key that supplies its value - not on a static definition table or an unrelated feature flag.
clusters.trigger: async_setup_entry iterates a module-level device-definition/params constant without checking the device's reported state, or appends an entity inside an `if` testing a capability key different from the datapoint key the entity description reads.
clusters.rationale: Entities created for datapoints the device does not have are permanently unknown, and gating on the wrong flag hides entities that do work; both mislead users about what their hardware supports.

clusters.rule: When the user step and the reauth (or reconfigure) step of a config flow run the same validation, share one implementation and branch on the flow source at the end, rather than duplicating the connect/validate block.
clusters.trigger: config_flow.py contains async_step_reauth_confirm whose try/except validation body duplicates async_step_user, differing only in async_create_entry vs async_update_reload_and_abort.
clusters.rationale: Duplicated validation drifts: a later fix to the error mapping in one step silently leaves the other step behind.

clusters.rule: A coordinator must not await one API call per device inside a for loop in _async_update_data; use the library's batch endpoint, or asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True) so per-item failures are isolated and previous values are kept for the items that errored.
clusters.trigger: _async_update_data awaits a client call inside a `for` loop over devices, circuits, zones or endpoints and assembles the results.
clusters.rationale: Sequential per-device polling multiplies request volume and refresh latency by the device count, and lets the first failing device abort the entire update for every other entity.

clusters.rule: Keep device- and API-specific data marshalling - timestamp formatting, vendor parameter string construction - in the upstream library rather than in the integration's coordinator or entity modules.
clusters.trigger: A coordinator or entity module defines helpers that format datetimes or build vendor-specific request parameter strings before handing them to the library client.
clusters.rationale: Home Assistant integrations are meant to be thin adapters; protocol details that change with the vendor API belong in the library that is versioned against it.

clusters.rule: Log expected and per-item failures at debug or warning level, never at warning-in-a-loop or _LOGGER.exception; reserve the higher levels for conditions the user can act on that cannot repeat once per polled item.
clusters.trigger: A _LOGGER.warning sits inside a loop over remote objects in an except branch that merely skips the item, or _LOGGER.exception is called in an except block of a coordinator update handling connection/HTTP errors.
clusters.rationale: The coordinator already reports update failures once; a stack trace or per-item warning every polling interval floods the log with noise the user cannot act on.

clusters.rule: A failing backup agent must fail only itself: an exception raised by one backup platform must not abort the overall backup or the other platforms, and the platform API contract is documented rather than defensively re-validated on every call.
clusters.trigger: Changes to the backup agent/platform API (agent.py, manager.py) that propagate a single agent's exception into the shared backup flow, or add per-call validation of platform-supplied callbacks.
clusters.rationale: Backups are the last line of defence; one misbehaving agent must never cost the user every other backup target.

clusters.rule: Do not silence a typing error with a blanket `# type: ignore`; give the value the correct type instead - cast it explicitly, build a properly typed structure, or add typing for the library function.
clusters.trigger: A return, assignment or registry call gains `# type: ignore[no-any-return]`, `[arg-type]` or `[comparison-overlap]` around a call into an untyped dependency or around device_entry.identifiers / async_update_device.
clusters.rationale: An ignore comment hides the mismatch instead of resolving it, so the next reader has no way to tell whether the value really has the type the surrounding code assumes.

clusters.rule: An entity lifecycle override must call the matching base-class hook - async_will_remove_from_hass calls super().async_will_remove_from_hass(); never satisfy the home-assistant-missing-super-call check by calling a different hook or by disabling it.
clusters.trigger: An overridden async_added_to_hass / async_will_remove_from_hass calls a super() method with a different name, or adds a pylint disable for home-assistant-missing-super-call.
clusters.rationale: The base hooks do real bookkeeping in both directions; calling the wrong one leaks the registration the correct one would have cleaned up.

clusters.rule: Create shared clients, sessions and derived per-entry values once in async_setup_entry, store them on entry.runtime_data and close them in async_unload_entry; platform modules and entities must consume that object rather than constructing or re-deriving their own copy.
clusters.trigger: An entity __init__ or helper instantiates a client/session/resolver of the type __init__.py already stores on runtime_data, or the same fetch-plus-assert block to narrow a client attribute appears in two or more platform modules of one integration.
clusters.rationale: One object per entry is what makes unload deterministic and keeps the narrowing assertions in a single place; duplicated construction leaks connections and duplicated derivation drifts.

clusters.rule: Call _abort_if_unique_id_mismatch with an explicit reason= argument matching an abort key in strings.json instead of relying on the default reason.
clusters.trigger: A reconfigure or reauth config-flow step calls self._abort_if_unique_id_mismatch() with no arguments.
clusters.rationale: The default reason gives the user a generic abort text that does not say which device they picked was wrong.

clusters.rule: Config flow steps, including discovery steps, must catch the same set of library exceptions the integration handles during entry setup - connection, timeout and authentication errors, TimeoutError included - and map each onto a specific errors key or abort reason such as cannot_connect, invalid_auth or not_found, rather than letting them escape or collapsing them into unknown.
clusters.trigger: A config-flow step awaits a library call with no except clause, catches only the library's own error base class while the coordinator also catches TimeoutError, or maps every failure to reason unknown.
clusters.rationale: The config flow is the only place the user can fix the problem, so it has to tell them which problem it is; an uncaught or unknown-mapped error just shows an unrecoverable dialog.

clusters.rule: Map device value ranges onto Home Assistant ranges with the shared range and percentage helpers the fan and light platforms already use, instead of hand-rolling a conversion table or arithmetic constant in const.py.
clusters.trigger: A new integration defines its own dict comprehension or arithmetic constant mapping device steps onto the 1-255 brightness range or a 0-100 percentage.
clusters.rationale: The shared helpers already handle rounding and edge values consistently across every integration; a private table diverges at the ends of the range.

clusters.rule: Do not optimistically assign _attr_* state and call async_write_ha_state after issuing a device command when the integration already registers a device callback that reports the new state.
clusters.trigger: async_turn_on/async_turn_off sends a command and then sets _attr_* and calls self.async_write_ha_state() in an integration that registers a device state callback.
clusters.rationale: The callback is the authority; writing a guessed state first makes the entity flicker and can leave it lying when the device rejects the command.

clusters.rule: Thread the ConfigEntry explicitly through discovery callbacks that run off the event loop instead of looking the entry or its runtime_data up from hass inside those callbacks.
clusters.trigger: A discovery helper or zeroconf/mDNS callback executing on a non-event-loop thread reaches into hass to find a config entry or its runtime_data.
clusters.rationale: hass.config_entries is not safe to inspect from another thread, and the entry the callback belongs to is known at registration time anyway.

clusters.rule: Reference existing translation text with the exact [%key:...%] reference syntax - including the shared [%key:common::config_flow::data::*%] entries for standard fields such as host, port, username, password and ssl - instead of repeating a label, data_description, or exception message that is already defined elsewhere; the reference path must contain no stray whitespace.
clusters.trigger: A strings.json diff adds a value textually identical to one already present under another step or section of the same file, or gives a plain literal label for a field that already exists under common::config_flow::data.
clusters.rationale: Duplicated strings are translated separately and then drift apart; the reference syntax keeps one source of truth and saves translator effort.

clusters.rule: Diagnostics must redact every identifying field the payload can contain - MAC addresses, serials and device identifiers as well as credentials - and must redact them everywhere they appear, including nested structures such as override target ids, not only in the collection that primarily lists them.
clusters.trigger: A diagnostics.py defines TO_REDACT covering keys, hosts and passwords while the config entry or fixtures also carry a MAC/serial, or wraps one collection in async_redact_data while returning a sibling structure verbatim that echoes the same ids.
clusters.rationale: Users paste diagnostics into public issues; an identifier that survives in one corner of the payload defeats the redaction everywhere else.

clusters.rule: Selector options presented in a config flow must carry a user-facing, translatable label instead of reusing the raw internal option value.
clusters.trigger: A config flow builds SelectOptionDict(value=X, label=X) or passes an internal constant straight through as the displayed label.
clusters.rationale: Internal constants are neither readable nor translatable, so the user picks from a list of implementation detail.

clusters.rule: A HomeAssistantError raised from an entity service handler must name the value that was rejected and, where a fixed set exists, the accepted values.
clusters.trigger: An entity service method raises HomeAssistantError with a bare static message such as `Invalid source` after a lookup against a mapping constant returns None.
clusters.rationale: The user wrote the value in an automation; without the rejected and the accepted values in the message they cannot tell what to change it to.

clusters.rule: Clamp incoming entity-service values to their documented Home Assistant range before converting them into device units.
clusters.trigger: async_set_volume_level or a similar service handler multiplies the incoming 0..1 float by a device range and offset without bounding it first.
clusters.rationale: A value slightly outside the documented range is turned into an out-of-range device command that the hardware may accept and act on.

clusters.rule: Do not override a base-entity property marked @final and silence the error with a type: ignore; add an explicit extension hook to the base class instead.
clusters.trigger: An in-tree entity subclass redefines a property the base class marks @final, accompanied by `# type: ignore[misc]`.
clusters.rationale: @final states that the base class owns the behaviour; overriding it anyway breaks the invariant for every other subclass and hides the need for a real extension point.

clusters.rule: A trigger transition predicate for cover-backed domains must handle the opening and closing states explicitly, because a cover reports those states before is_closed is consulted and is_closed may still be None then.
clusters.trigger: An is_valid_transition in a domain trigger.py compares ATTR_IS_CLOSED between from_state and to_state for COVER_DOMAIN entities without handling STATE_OPENING/STATE_CLOSING or a None is_closed.
clusters.rationale: Covers pass through a moving state on every operation, so a predicate that only compares the closed attribute either misses the transition or crashes on None.

clusters.rule: A dhcp discovery block in manifest.json that matches on hostname should also declare registered_devices, so devices already in the device registry are still matched by MAC when their hostname differs.
clusters.trigger: manifest.json gains a `dhcp` array whose entries only contain hostname or macaddress matchers, with no registered_devices flag.
clusters.rationale: Users rename their devices; without registered_devices a known device stops being rediscovered as soon as its hostname no longer matches the pattern.

clusters.rule: async_unload_entry must await async_unload_platforms first and only stop or close runtime resources when that call returned True, returning the same value.
clusters.trigger: async_unload_entry awaits a stop/close/disconnect on entry.runtime_data before calling async_unload_platforms, or ignores the boolean it returns.
clusters.rationale: Entities are still alive until the platforms unload; closing the connection first makes them fail on their way out, and discarding the boolean reports a successful unload that did not happen.

clusters.rule: Log messages must not repeat the integration name, brand or domain - the logger prefix already carries it.
clusters.trigger: A _LOGGER call's message string contains the integration's brand or domain name.
clusters.rationale: Every record is already prefixed with the module path, so the repetition only makes log lines longer.

clusters.rule: The field keys under services.<service>.fields in strings.json must correspond exactly to the fields that service declares in services.yaml - add a field to both files or to neither.
clusters.trigger: strings.json adds or keeps a field entry under one service while that service's block in services.yaml has no matching field key.
clusters.rationale: services.yaml defines the form and strings.json names it; a key present in only one of them is either an untranslated field or dead translation text.

clusters.rule: Default polling intervals for local-polling integrations belong in the 30-60 second range; a SCAN_INTERVAL or update_interval under roughly 30 seconds must be justified or made configurable.
clusters.trigger: A coordinator module sets SCAN_INTERVAL or DataUpdateCoordinator(update_interval=...) to a timedelta below about 30 seconds.
clusters.rationale: Every installation pays this cost forever on hardware the developer does not own; the default has to be the conservative one.

clusters.rule: When a trigger platform is adapted from another domain, rewrite its comments and stated rationale to describe the new domain's entities rather than the domain it was copied from.
clusters.trigger: A new homeassistant/components/<domain>/trigger.py contains comments naming a different domain's entity.
clusters.rationale: A leftover comment about buttons inside an event trigger sends the next reader looking for behaviour that is not there.

clusters.rule: A config flow that holds a live device connection must clear the client reference immediately after an explicit disconnect on the success path, so the flow's finally block or async_remove does not disconnect a second time.
clusters.trigger: A config_flow step awaits self._client.disconnect()/close() before async_create_entry while a finally block or async_remove also tears down self._client.
clusters.rationale: The second teardown runs against an already closed client and surfaces as an exception in a flow that otherwise succeeded.

clusters.rule: A subentry reconfigure flow must schedule the parent entry reload explicitly rather than depending on the config entry update listener, which does not exist while the entry is unloaded or in SETUP_RETRY.
clusters.trigger: A subentry flow calls async_update_and_abort or async_update_entry and relies on an update listener registered in async_setup_entry to apply the change.
clusters.rationale: The listener is registered by setup, so exactly in the failure state the user is trying to fix, nothing applies their new configuration.

clusters.rule: Filter config_entry.subentries by subentry_type before counting or iterating them; never treat the whole subentries mapping as one type.
clusters.trigger: Code uses len(self.config_entry.subentries) or iterates config_entry.subentries.values() without comparing subentry.subentry_type against the expected type constant.
clusters.rationale: An entry may carry several subentry types, so an unfiltered count or loop silently includes another feature's subentries.

clusters.rule: Do not call hass.async_add_executor_job once per item inside a loop or comprehension; collect the blocking work into a single function and schedule that on the executor one time.
clusters.trigger: await hass.async_add_executor_job(...) appears inside a for-loop, a list comprehension, or a comprehension condition.
clusters.rationale: Each call costs a thread hand-off and a context switch, so a per-entity loop turns one blocking read into dozens of round trips through the executor.

clusters.rule: Values assigned to context[title_placeholders] in a discovery config-flow step must not repeat punctuation the flow_title template already supplies; add a separate placeholder instead of embedding a parenthesised name inside the name placeholder.
clusters.trigger: A discovery step sets self.context title_placeholders to an f-string containing parentheses while strings.json defines flow_title with its own parenthesised placeholder.
clusters.rationale: The template and the placeholder each add their own brackets, so the discovered device shows up with doubled punctuation in the UI.

clusters.rule: A config flow must validate the connection by calling the same third-party library client the coordinator uses; it must not re-implement API paths, endpoints or response parsing inline.
clusters.trigger: config_flow.py builds a URL path, issues aiohttp/requests calls, or parses the API payload itself instead of instantiating the integration's client class and calling its method.
clusters.rationale: A flow that talks to the API by hand validates against a different code path than setup, so a configuration it accepts can still fail at runtime.

clusters.rule: manifest.json must list only keys the integration actually uses; empty placeholder keys such as an empty requirements, ssdp, zeroconf, homekit or dependencies value must be deleted rather than left empty.
clusters.trigger: A new or edited manifest.json contains a key whose value is an empty list or empty object.
clusters.rationale: An empty discovery or requirements key reads as a declared capability that does not exist and clutters every manifest diff after it.

clusters.rule: Integration API wrappers must not add their own HTTP status-code branches for 4xx, 429 or 5xx responses when the shared Home Assistant helper layer already maps those responses onto ConfigEntryAuthFailed or ConfigEntryNotReady.
clusters.trigger: api.py or a session/auth helper inspects ex.status ranges on a ClientResponseError and raises a config-entry exception the framework already raises.
clusters.rationale: Duplicating the framework's mapping means two places decide what a 401 means, and they will disagree after the next core change.

clusters.rule: async_get_config_entry_diagnostics must expose the redacted runtime coordinator data, not just the redacted config entry, when the integration claims the diagnostics quality-scale rule.
clusters.trigger: A diagnostics.py returns only the redacted config_entry while quality_scale.yaml marks diagnostics as done and runtime_data holds coordinator state.
clusters.rationale: Diagnostics exist to debug what the device reported; the config entry alone tells a maintainer nothing they did not already know.

clusters.rule: The pull request description must match what the diff actually does: it must not claim a removal, payload or quality-scale rule the code does not carry out, must not close an issue the change does not implement, and must cover every entity or behaviour the diff adds beyond the stated feature.
clusters.trigger: A PR body announces removing a key, adding data, or satisfying a quality-scale rule that the diff does not do; carries issue-closing keywords on a change that only bumps a requirement; or the diff adds entity descriptions or platform entities the title and body never mention.
clusters.rationale: The description is what reviewers and the release notes rely on; when it diverges from the diff, both the review and the changelog describe a change that was never made.

clusters.rule: When a coroutine is converted to a plain def helper, its docstring must stop describing it as a coroutine.
clusters.trigger: A diff changes `async def` to `def`, or adds a `def` helper, whose docstring still uses coroutine wording while the body never awaits.
clusters.rationale: Callers decide whether to await based on the docstring; a stale one invites an await on a plain function.

clusters.rule: A targeted refresh path in hassio that updates one object's state must also update every shared hass.data key derived from it that other coordinators read, not only the coordinator's own data.
clusters.trigger: A force/partial refresh helper writes to a coordinator's own data or a single DATA_* key while another coordinator in the same integration keys its work off a different DATA_* list that the helper leaves stale.
clusters.rationale: The two coordinators disagree about the same object until the next full refresh, which is exactly the window the targeted refresh was added to cover.

clusters.rule: system_health_info must never raise on an unexpected API payload type: coerce values fetched from Supervisor or another external API before formatting them, and skip the field on ValueError/TypeError.
clusters.trigger: system_health.py applies a numeric format spec, arithmetic or rounding directly to a value read out of an external info dict with .get().
clusters.rationale: The system health panel is the page a user opens when something is already broken; it must degrade to a missing field rather than fail to render.

clusters.rule: Use Core and Supervisor terminology precisely in docstrings and user-facing text: a repair is a Core concept, while the Supervisor raises an issue and a suggestion; do not attribute a repair to the Supervisor.
clusters.trigger: A docstring, comment, log line or string says the Supervisor raises or creates a repair, or otherwise mixes Core repair vocabulary with Supervisor issue/suggestion vocabulary.
clusters.rationale: The two systems are separate and users are directed to different UI for each; blurring the words sends people to the wrong place.

clusters.rule: Entries added to the homematicip_cloud unique-id migration map must supply every field the migration helper needs, including an explicit channel for single-channel devices, so no entry makes the helper return None and leave entities unmigrated.
clusters.trigger: Entries are added to UNIQUE_ID_MIGRATION_MAP omitting a field the _migrate_unique_id helper requires to build the new unique id, so its fallback returns None.
clusters.rationale: A silently skipped migration leaves those entities on the old unique id with no error anywhere, and the user loses their history.

clusters.rule: A light must preserve its last brightness: async_turn_on may only default to full brightness for a bare turn-on with no attributes and must keep the current level when the call supplies only effect or colour, and async_turn_off must not zero or clear the brightness attribute.
clusters.trigger: async_turn_on initialises brightness to a constant and overwrites it only when ATTR_BRIGHTNESS is in kwargs, or async_turn_off sets self._attr_brightness = 0 or resets another level attribute.
clusters.rationale: Users expect a light to come back at the level they left it; clobbering the stored level on either side of the cycle throws that away.

clusters.rule: Optional values must be omitted from config entry data rather than stored as None; build the data dict conditionally instead of always writing the key.
clusters.trigger: async_create_entry or async_update_entry passes a data dict that always includes an optional key such as CONF_PASSWORD whose value may be None.
clusters.rationale: A stored None is indistinguishable from a value the user cleared, and every reader then has to handle both the missing key and the null.

clusters.rule: Helpers that are imported across module boundaries - by another integration module or by the tests - must have public names; do not export underscore-prefixed functions.
clusters.trigger: A new `def _name(...)` in const.py or another shared module is imported from coordinator.py, a platform module, or tests/.
clusters.rationale: The underscore is the signal that a name is private to its module; importing it elsewhere makes the marker a lie.

clusters.rule: State flags that gate issue-registry calls must be initialised to their real starting value (False), not None, so the first coordinator refresh does not read the initial state as a transition and delete an issue that was never created.
clusters.trigger: A coordinator declares a tracking attribute as `bool | None = None` and compares it against a freshly computed boolean to choose between async_create_issue and async_delete_issue.
clusters.rationale: A None sentinel differs from every real value, so the very first refresh always looks like a change and fires a registry call for a state nothing had.

clusters.rule: Do not add another per-refresh client call inside a coordinator's _async_update_data; obtain the extra field from the existing bulk call, bundle the requests, or document the added request cost.
clusters.trigger: A diff adds a new awaited client call inside _async_update_data alongside the existing client calls.
clusters.rationale: Every added call runs on every polling interval for every install, so a second request doubles the load on the device or the vendor API.

clusters.rule: Entity names in strings.json must read as a natural sentence-cased phrase rather than a prefixed label with a colon, and related keys should share a common suffix instead of a common prefix.
clusters.trigger: New entity name entries whose values share a leading word plus colon, or whose keys share a leading token such as an alarm_ prefix.
clusters.rationale: The frontend already groups entities by device, so a repeated prefix is noise; a natural phrase sorts and reads better in every list.

clusters.rule: Do not splat a remote payload dict into an event entity's attributes; nest it under a dedicated data key so payload keys cannot overwrite reserved attributes.
clusters.trigger: _trigger_event or event attribute construction merges the remote payload into the top-level attribute dict.
clusters.rationale: A remote sender then controls reserved attribute names on the entity, which is both a correctness and a trust problem.

clusters.rule: Do not set _attr_translation_key on an entity whose device class already yields the correct default name; rely on the device-class default translation instead.
clusters.trigger: A new entity class sets _attr_device_class together with an _attr_translation_key whose meaning merely restates that device class.
clusters.rationale: The device-class default is already translated into every language; a redundant key adds translator work for the same word.

clusters.rule: Schedule integration background work with entry.async_create_background_task or entry.async_create_task rather than hass.async_create_task, so the task is tracked and cancelled when the config entry unloads.
clusters.trigger: hass.async_create_task( is called from integration setup, a coordinator listener, or any entry-scoped callback.
clusters.rationale: A task owned by hass outlives the entry, so unloading or reloading the integration leaves the old task running against a dead client.

clusters.rule: Anything interpolated into a user-facing error message or into translation_placeholders must be a deterministic, informative string: never a raw container repr such as str(set) or str(dict), never the repr of a bare wrapper exception instead of the underlying library error or its __cause__, and never an exception whose str() is empty - fall back to the exception type name.
clusters.trigger: A raise builds translation_placeholders from str() of a set/list/dict, formats an exception that was itself raised bare with `raise CustomError from err`, or interpolates an exception such as TimeoutError that stringifies to an empty value.
clusters.rationale: These strings are the only thing the user sees when setup fails; a Python repr, a blank message, or a wrapper with no detail leaves them with nothing to act on and makes bug reports useless.

clusters.rule: Media source identifier parsing and service helpers must validate their inputs and preconditions before use and raise a proper Home Assistant error - Unresolvable/BrowseError, ServiceValidationError or HomeAssistantError - so a malformed identifier, an unloaded config entry, or an uncastable user value never surfaces as a raw UnboundLocalError, AttributeError, ValueError or TypeError.
clusters.trigger: A from_identifier/async_resolve_media splits an identifier and assigns fields without checking the parts exist; code reads entry.runtime_data after async_get_entry without checking the entry is loaded; or an entity service passes a user-provided value straight into int()/float()/an enum lookup or a library call with no try/except.
clusters.rationale: These paths are all reachable from user input, and a raw Python exception gives the user a traceback instead of a message telling them what they typed wrong.

clusters.rule: Do not re-scan hass.config_entries for an entry that a helper on the same code path already resolved; return the entry from that helper or call async_entry_for_domain_unique_id once.
clusters.trigger: A loop over config entries or a repeated async_entry_for_domain_unique_id call follows a helper that already looked the same entry up.
clusters.rationale: The lookup walks every entry in the system and the answer is already in hand one frame up the stack.

clusters.rule: Never suppress asyncio.CancelledError around long-lived awaits in a coordinator; catch it explicitly, cancel and await the pending future, then re-raise when the current task is genuinely being cancelled.
clusters.trigger: A suppress(...) contextmanager including asyncio.CancelledError, or `except asyncio.CancelledError: pass`, wrapping an awaited long-poll or IDLE future.
clusters.rationale: Swallowing cancellation makes the task un-killable, so unloading the entry hangs and the shutdown never completes.

clusters.rule: Integrations must not read private attributes of Home Assistant core helper objects; use a public API, or document why none exists and what upstream change would break the access.
clusters.trigger: An underscore-prefixed attribute access on a core object, typically marked with `# noqa: SLF001`.
clusters.rationale: Private core internals change without notice and without a deprecation path, so the integration breaks on a release that promised nothing.

clusters.rule: A sensor's state_class must match the nature of its value: declare one, consistent with the integration's sibling descriptions of the same device_class, for genuinely numeric readings; do not put a numeric state class on a value that can also be a non-numeric enum state, and do not use SensorStateClass.MEASUREMENT for uptime or duration-since-boot sensors.
clusters.trigger: A SensorEntityDescription sets device_class and unit but omits state_class while neighbouring descriptions set one; assigns MEASUREMENT/TOTAL* to a key whose strings.json also defines enum state values; or combines SensorDeviceClass.DURATION or an uptime translation_key with MEASUREMENT.
clusters.rationale: state_class is what enrolls a sensor in long-term statistics; missing it loses the history, and a wrong one records statistics for values that are not measurements at all.

clusters.rule: Do device registration and stale-device cleanup once in the coordinator's _async_setup, not in _async_update_data.
clusters.trigger: Device registry writes or an async_cleanup_stale_devices call made from _async_update_data.
clusters.rationale: The update method runs on every polling interval; registry work belongs to setup and repeating it costs writes on every refresh.

clusters.rule: When an entity description's key is renamed, update the matching translation_key and its strings.json entries, or document in a comment why the old translation key is deliberately kept.
clusters.trigger: A diff changes the key= of an entity description but leaves the adjacent translation_key= unchanged.
clusters.rationale: Key and translation_key are read together by anyone maintaining the file; an unexplained mismatch looks like an oversight even when it is intentional.

clusters.rule: manifest.json requirements must match what the code actually needs: every third-party module the integration imports has to be declared, and the pinned version must be new enough to provide every attribute and method the code calls - bump the pin in the same PR.
clusters.trigger: A diff adds or changes a top-level import of a non-stdlib, non-homeassistant module with no matching requirements change, or uses a client attribute or method the pinned version does not provide.
clusters.rationale: The manifest is what actually gets installed, so an undeclared or too-old requirement fails at import or attribute access on every user's system while it works on the developer's.

clusters.rule: A legacy YAML platform reduced to an import or repair-issue stub must still report successful setup - return a no-op service or True rather than None - so the legacy platform helper does not log a setup failure.
clusters.trigger: async_get_service, async_get_scanner or a comparable legacy platform entry point is rewritten to only create an issue or start an import flow and then return None.
clusters.rationale: Returning None is the helper's failure signal, so a user who is being told to migrate also gets an unrelated setup error in their log.

clusters.rule: Handle the import flow's abort reasons before raising the deprecated_yaml repair issue, so a failed import does not tell the user their YAML was successfully migrated.
clusters.trigger: A YAML import path calls async_create_issue with translation_key deprecated_yaml unconditionally after starting an import flow, without branching on the flow's abort reason.
clusters.rationale: The repair issue instructs the user to delete their YAML; issuing it after a failed import destroys the only working configuration they had.

clusters.rule: Do not abort a reconfigure flow on unique-id mismatch when the existing entry still carries the integration's legacy unique_id; match the legacy value and migrate the entry to the new scheme.
clusters.trigger: A config flow computes a new-style unique id, calls async_set_unique_id and then _abort_if_unique_id_mismatch in the SOURCE_RECONFIGURE branch, in a diff that changes how the unique id is derived.
clusters.rationale: Every existing install still holds the old id, so the mismatch check turns a unique-id change into a permanent abort for users who did nothing wrong.

clusters.rule: Never assign to a config flow's VERSION or MINOR_VERSION at runtime; they are class-level constants describing the entry schema, and migrations must be driven by async_migrate_entry.
clusters.trigger: A diff contains self.VERSION = ... or self.MINOR_VERSION = ... inside a config-flow step or handler body.
clusters.rationale: The class attribute is what the migration machinery compares against; mutating it per instance makes the stored version meaningless.

clusters.rule: Reserve the async_ / _async_ prefix for coroutine functions and event-loop callbacks; rename synchronous helpers to a plain _setup_*-style name.
clusters.trigger: A diff adds a `def _async_foo(...)` or `def async_foo(...)` that is not `async def` and contains no await.
clusters.rationale: The prefix is the codebase-wide signal that a call has to be awaited; a synchronous function wearing it produces coroutine-never-awaited bugs at every call site.

clusters.rule: Do not name a variable `platform` when it holds an entity domain such as switch or select; call it domain or entity_domain and keep `platform` for the Home Assistant platform concept.
clusters.trigger: A loop variable or parameter named platform is assigned entity-domain strings and passed to registry helpers.
clusters.rationale: Platform and domain are distinct concepts in core, and registry helpers take one of each; conflating the names is how the wrong one gets passed.

clusters.rule: An entity's state property must read the same field its command method writes; after a successful command, update the entity's own state and write it rather than waiting for a library field that may not refresh.
clusters.trigger: A state property such as current_option or is_on reads one library attribute while async_select_option/async_turn_* sets a different one, with no async_write_ha_state of the new value.
clusters.rationale: The command appears to do nothing in the UI because the property is still reading the field nobody updated.

clusters.rule: Do not add per-update lookups that can only ever apply to a subset of devices; gate them behind a setup-time check or a cached reference so unaffected devices pay nothing on each update.
clusters.trigger: An available or update path unconditionally performs a topology lookup such as get_compose_parent(...) plus an attribute read on every invocation.
clusters.rationale: This runs for every entity on every attribute change in a large mesh, to answer a question that is fixed at setup time for almost all of them.

clusters.rule: In the Matter entity base, make availability precedence explicit when combining a bridged or composed parent's Reachable with the child endpoint's own: return the parent's verdict directly instead of falling through to the child's attribute.
clusters.trigger: An available property checks a parent endpoint's Reachable attribute and then continues on to read the child endpoint's Reachable when the parent is reachable.
clusters.rationale: The fall-through leaves it ambiguous which endpoint decided the entity was available, which is exactly the confusion the parent check was added to remove.

clusters.rule: When deserializing stored KNX telegram values, accept every payload type the DPT layer can produce - str for DPT 16, dict for DPTComplex - rather than narrowing to numeric and bool types.
clusters.trigger: A restore or serialization path filters telegram payloads with isinstance(value, (int, float, bool)) or a similarly narrow type check.
clusters.rationale: The narrow check silently drops the payloads it does not recognise, so those telegrams disappear from the restored history.

clusters.rule: A change that alters behaviour users may already depend on - including rerouting an existing device or event action to a different action type - must be declared as a breaking change in the PR description and release notes, even when it is the intended bug fix.
clusters.trigger: A diff changes existing runtime behaviour (initial coordinator data, default values, emitted states) or maps a previously unhandled event type to a new action constant, in a PR whose description has no breaking-change section.
clusters.rationale: Users' automations are built on the old behaviour; the release notes are the only place they find out why their automation stopped firing.

clusters.rule: Filesystem traversal in media_source search must stream lazily and stop at the result cap instead of materializing or sorting the whole tree.
clusters.trigger: A diff calls sorted(path.rglob(...)) or otherwise builds a complete list of filesystem entries before a result limit such as MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS is applied.
clusters.rationale: Users point media directories at whole libraries; walking and sorting every file to return ten results blocks for seconds on each search.

clusters.rule: Coordinators must read configuration values off the config entry they already receive (entry.data[CONF_*]) instead of accepting the same values as extra constructor parameters.
clusters.trigger: A DataUpdateCoordinator subclass __init__ takes values such as latitude, longitude or host as parameters while also being handed the ConfigEntry those values come from.
clusters.rationale: Two sources for the same value drift when the entry is updated, and the constructor signature grows with every option.

clusters.rule: A library call added to a coordinator's periodic update path must handle transient errors the same way the sibling calls around it do, so one failed poll does not propagate out of _async_update_data.
clusters.trigger: A new device/API command is added inside a coordinator method that runs every update interval, without the error suppression the adjacent calls use.
clusters.rationale: The neighbouring calls already established what a transient failure means here; the odd one out turns a routine timeout into a whole-integration update failure.

clusters.rule: Value callables declared on custom EntityDescription subclasses must be typed with StateType, extended with datetime where needed, rather than a hand-narrowed return union.
clusters.trigger: A SensorEntityDescription or EntityDescription subclass declares a value or value_fn field typed as a partial state union such as Callable[..., str | float | None].
clusters.rationale: StateType is the type the entity actually returns; a narrower union has to be widened again the first time a description needs another state type.

clusters.rule: A new integration's initial quality_scale.yaml must already list the silver, gold and platinum rules, not just the bronze tier.
clusters.trigger: A newly added quality_scale.yaml contains only bronze-tier rule entries.
clusters.rationale: The full list is what makes the remaining work visible; omitting the higher tiers hides the todos instead of recording them.

clusters.rule: MQTT command templates must be rendered with the same object that is supplied as the `value` template variable; do not pass a pre-serialized payload alongside the raw variables.
clusters.trigger: A call through MqttCommandTemplate/async_render passes a json-dumped payload while also supplying the raw object as the value template variable.
clusters.rationale: The template author sees one shape and the default path emits another, so a user template and the default disagree about what was sent.

clusters.rule: Config-flow steps must not add a separate connectivity probe when an API call already made in that step proves the service is reachable and the user's selection is valid.
clusters.trigger: A config flow step adds an _async_test_connection()-style call after another call in the same step already queried the same API to validate user input.
clusters.rationale: The extra round trip only slows the flow down and adds a second place where the error mapping can disagree with the first.

clusters.rule: Entities that expose technical or diagnostic data must set _attr_entity_category = EntityCategory.DIAGNOSTIC, satisfying the entity-category quality-scale rule.
clusters.trigger: A new entity carrying technical information (feed status, last update time, upstream ids) is added with no entity_category, while quality_scale.yaml still lists entity-category as todo.
clusters.rationale: Without the category these entities land in the user's main dashboard next to the readings they actually care about.

clusters.rule: A service parameter that requires a newer backend must check the connected server's schema_version (or the equivalent capability field) and raise a translated ServiceValidationError before the parameter is used.
clusters.trigger: A service handler reads a newly added parameter and forwards it to the library with no explicit version guard.
clusters.rationale: Users run older servers than the integration supports; without the guard they get an opaque library error instead of being told to upgrade.

clusters.rule: Optional service and config values validated with cv.string must be tested with `is not None`, never for truthiness, because the empty string is accepted input.
clusters.trigger: A handler writes `if call.data.get(ATTR_X):` or another bare truthiness check for a key whose voluptuous schema is cv.string.
clusters.rationale: The schema admits the empty string as a deliberate value, and a truthiness check silently treats it as not supplied.

clusters.rule: Code comments must describe the code as it stands; the reason a change was made belongs in the pull request, not in a comment left behind in the source.
clusters.trigger: A diff adds a comment that narrates the edit itself, for example explaining what an older dependency version used to render or why an existing value is being preserved.
clusters.rationale: The comment stops making sense the moment the change is history, and the PR is where that reasoning is searchable.

clusters.rule: Pull requests must fill in the Proposed change section and tick a Type of change box, particularly when the diff alters config-flow behaviour.
clusters.trigger: A PR body leaves the template's Proposed change section empty or selects no Type of change checkbox, while the diff changes user-visible setup behaviour.
clusters.rationale: Reviewers and the release-notes tooling both read those sections; an empty one means the change ships undescribed.

clusters.rule: Once an integration defines a ConfigEntry type alias carrying its runtime data, every function that takes that entry must be annotated with the alias rather than plain ConfigEntry.
clusters.trigger: A diff introduces a ConfigEntry type alias but leaves async_setup_entry/async_unload_entry or helper functions annotated with the bare ConfigEntry type.
clusters.rationale: The alias is what makes entry.runtime_data typed; a bare annotation gives up that checking in exactly the functions that use it.

clusters.rule: Timing behaviour introduced by a fix must be covered by a test that patches the module's asyncio.sleep and asserts the delay, not only by tests counting calls.
clusters.trigger: A diff adds an inter-command delay, pause or retry backoff while the accompanying tests only assert how many commands were sent.
clusters.rationale: A call-count test passes with the delay removed, so nothing stops the next refactor from deleting the thing the fix was about.

clusters.rule: Coordinator subclasses must not re-annotate the inherited config_entry attribute; pass config_entry=None to super().__init__ and leave the base class type intact.
clusters.trigger: A DataUpdateCoordinator subclass body declares `config_entry: None` or otherwise narrows the annotation of config_entry.
clusters.rationale: The base class owns that attribute's type; narrowing it in a subclass breaks the substitutability the coordinator helpers rely on.

clusters.rule: When a service option lets the user pick a combination of values, expose it as a select selector with multiple: true rather than inventing a synthetic combined option such as `both`, matching the selector shape sibling integrations already use for the same service.
clusters.trigger: A services.yaml diff adds or edits a select selector whose options list contains an aggregate value (both, all, any) alongside the individual values.
clusters.rationale: The multi-select shape is what the frontend and every comparable service already use, and it scales when a third value is added.

clusters.rule: Name a module-level tuple of EntityDescription objects after the platform it populates (SENSOR_DESCRIPTIONS, SELECT_TYPES), not after one entity or one subset of the entities it contains.
clusters.trigger: A platform module declares an EntityDescription tuple constant named after a single entity, or a diff adds descriptions to an existing one so the constant now covers more than its name implies.
clusters.rationale: The constant is the platform's whole description table; a name tied to one entry misleads the next person adding to it.

clusters.rule: Build the diagnostics payload by serialising a known, explicit set of fields from the coordinator or client data: do not walk arbitrary object graphs with a generic recursive JSON-coercion layer, do not probe with hasattr/getattr or invoke callables found on the object, and do not fall back to a default repr/str rendering that embeds memory addresses.
clusters.trigger: diagnostics.py adds a recursive coercion helper with depth limits or type fallbacks, calls anything it finds callable on a client/device object, or formats unknown objects into the payload through an f-string or str() fallback.
clusters.rationale: Reflective diagnostics can execute arbitrary device-object methods and produce output that differs between runs, which makes the payload both unsafe and useless for snapshot comparison.

clusters.rule: Production integration code must not detect or branch on test doubles; fix the fixture or the test instead of adding mock-aware code paths under homeassistant/components/.
clusters.trigger: A file under homeassistant/components/ references mock_add_spec, unittest.mock, MagicMock, or otherwise special-cases behaviour when the object appears to be a mock.
clusters.rationale: The branch means the shipped path is not the one the tests exercise, so the tests stop being evidence about production behaviour.

clusters.rule: During async_setup_entry, configure the library client so connection and auth exceptions propagate instead of being swallowed by a client-side suppress-errors mode, so setup can raise ConfigEntryNotReady or an auth failure; keep the suppressing mode for the post-setup refresh loop only.
clusters.trigger: __init__.py constructs the API client for setup with a flag that suppresses or only logs exceptions, then wraps the first call in try/except.
clusters.rationale: A suppressed setup error becomes a loaded entry with no data instead of a retry or a reauth prompt, so the user sees a broken integration with no explanation.

clusters.rule: Config-flow credential validation that iterates a listing endpoint must treat an empty result as a validation failure and set an errors key rather than creating the entry, and async_setup_entry must apply the same check.
clusters.trigger: config_flow.py validates the connection by iterating an API listing and only treats raised exceptions as failure.
clusters.rationale: An empty listing means the credentials reach nothing usable, so accepting it creates an entry that can only ever be empty.

clusters.rule: Import a library's exception classes from one module path consistently across the integration and its tests, and confirm that path is actually exported by the version pinned in manifest.json.
clusters.trigger: A PR bumps a library and adds imports of its exception types, with the integration importing from the package root while the tests import the same names from a submodule, or vice versa.
